sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报杂志》的撰稿人，主要撰写科学和技术方面的文章。

sentences.en: This week's Sunday Read is a story I wrote for the magazine's space issue about the space force.
sentences.zh: 本周的“周日阅读”是我为杂志太空专刊撰写的一篇关于太空军的故事。

sentences.en: It's the newest, smallest, and most secretive branch of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 它是美国最新、规模最小、也最神秘的军种。

sentences.en: military.
sentences.zh: 军队。

sentences.en: It was established just four years ago and its members, they're called guardians,
sentences.zh: 它成立于四年前，其成员被称为“守护者”，

sentences.en: are in charge of observing and protecting everything that belongs to America that's orbiting above the earth.
sentences.zh: 负责监视和保护所有属于美国且在地球轨道上运行的资产。

sentences.en: That includes defending military satellites and all the satellites we sometimes take for granted that are vital to our day-to-day lives.
sentences.zh: 这包括保卫军事卫星，以及我们有时视为理所当然、但对日常生活至关重要的所有卫星。

sentences.en: Unlike, say, the Air Force or even the Coast Guard, you won't see photos of its planes and ships in service.
sentences.zh: 与空军甚至海岸警卫队不同，你不会看到其飞机和舰船服役的照片。

sentences.en: And because so much of its work is out of sight, the space force has almost become this caricature.
sentences.zh: 正因为其大部分工作都在视线之外，太空军几乎成了一种讽刺的形象。

sentences.en: There's even a Netflix comedy series about it starring Steve Carell.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一部由史蒂夫·卡瑞尔主演的Netflix喜剧系列剧以此为题材。

sentences.en: The operating costs for the space force amount to about $26 billion a year.
sentences.zh: 太空军的年度运营成本约为260亿美元。

sentences.en: And I don't think it's uncommon to hear questions like, well, why do we need to spend so much to protect our satellites?
sentences.zh: 我认为听到这样的问题并不罕见：好吧，为什么我们需要花这么多钱来保护我们的卫星？

sentences.en: Or, are these threats to our satellites real or imagined?
sentences.zh: 或者，这些对我们卫星的威胁是真实的还是想象出来的？

sentences.en: But, picture life without GPS, without mapping and directions, or without weather satellites, which our entire agricultural systems depend on.
sentences.zh: 但是，想象一下没有GPS、没有地图和导航、或者没有我们整个农业系统所依赖的气象卫星的生活。

sentences.en: Our lives are tied very intimately to what's happening in space.
sentences.zh: 我们的生活与太空中发生的事情息息相关。

sentences.en: And so, I wanted to find out, what does this new branch of the military actually do?
sentences.zh: 因此，我想弄清楚，这个新的军种到底是做什么的？

sentences.en: And how do they do it?
sentences.zh: 他们又是如何运作的？

sentences.en: So, after approaching the space force and explaining the premise of my story, they agreed to give me some access that I think they don't ordinarily offer.
sentences.zh: 所以，在接触太空军并解释了我的报道前提后，他们同意给我提供一些我认为他们通常不会提供的访问权限。

sentences.en: In Colorado, I visited the Peterson and Schriever bases, which were formerly used by the Air Force.
sentences.zh: 在科罗拉多州，我参观了彼得森基地和施里弗基地，这些基地以前由空军使用。

sentences.en: I also went to a place called Space Systems Command in Los Angeles, not far from LAX.
sentences.zh: 我还去了洛杉矶一个叫太空系统司令部的地方，离洛杉矶国际机场不远。

sentences.en: Most of the time, there was a great veil of secrecy over what the Guardians were doing.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，守护者们所做的工作都笼罩在巨大的保密面纱之下。

sentences.en: At Peterson, I couldn't bring any electronic devices into the buildings.
sentences.zh: 在彼得森基地，我不能带任何电子设备进入大楼。

sentences.en: I could only go old school and use a notebook.
sentences.zh: 我只能回归传统，使用笔记本。

sentences.en: There were some people I couldn't quote by name.
sentences.zh: 有些人的名字我不能引用。

sentences.en: And sometimes I'd enter a room and it would need to be vacated before I could walk through it.
sentences.zh: 有时我走进一个房间，在我穿过之前，房间必须清空。

sentences.en: And I'd have to pass through quickly.
sentences.zh: 而且我必须快速通过。

sentences.en: But I did uncover a lot in my reporting about how and why the Space Force operates, which you'll hear about in my story.
sentences.zh: 但在我的报道中，我确实揭示了许多关于太空军如何运作以及为何运作的内容，你将在我的故事中听到。

sentences.en: One of the most striking things to me was this.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，最令人震惊的事情之一是这个。

sentences.en: I've always thought of space as a place of wonder and delight and endless curiosity.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为太空是一个充满奇迹、愉悦和无尽好奇心的地方。

sentences.en: But the Space Force Guardians, in their own words, consider space to be a contested, congested, war-fighting domain.
sentences.zh: 但太空军的守护者们用他们自己的话来说，认为太空是一个充满竞争、拥挤的作战领域。

sentences.en: This military branch of about 15,000 people has to prepare for a war in space, even as they do everything they can to prevent a war in space.
sentences.zh: 这个拥有约15,000人的军种必须为太空战争做准备，即使他们正在尽一切努力防止太空战争的发生。

sentences.en: It's this delicate balancing act between security and the kind of arms race we've entered into with Russia and China.
sentences.zh: 这是安全与我们与俄罗斯和中国之间陷入的那种军备竞赛之间微妙的平衡行为。

sentences.en: And they have to make sure they don't overstep it.
sentences.zh: 他们必须确保自己不会越界。

sentences.en: So, here's my article.
sentences.zh: 那么，这就是我的文章。

sentences.en: Read by Eric Jason Martin.
sentences.zh: 由埃里克·杰森·马丁朗读。

sentences.en: Chief Master Sergeant Ron Lurch of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国太空军的首席军士长罗恩·勒奇

sentences.en: Space Force sat down in his office in Los Angeles one morning in September to deliver a briefing known as a threat assessment.
sentences.zh: 9月的一个早晨，在洛杉矶的办公室里坐下来，进行了一次被称为“威胁评估”的简报。

sentences.en: The current threats in space are less sci-fi than you might expect, but there are a surprising number of them.
sentences.zh: 目前太空中的威胁并不像你想象的那么科幻，但数量却惊人。

sentences.en: At least 44,500 space objects now circle Earth, including 9,000 active satellites and 19,000 significant pieces of debris.
sentences.zh: 目前至少有44,500个太空物体环绕地球，包括9,000颗现役卫星和19,000块重要的碎片。

sentences.en: What's most concerning isn't the swarm of satellites, but the types.
sentences.zh: 最令人担忧的不是卫星的数量，而是它们的类型。

sentences.en: We know that there are kinetic kill vehicles, Lurch said.
sentences.zh: “我们知道存在动能杀伤武器，”勒奇说。

sentences.en: For example, a Russian nesting doll satellite, in which a big satellite releases a tiny one, and the tiny one releases a mechanism that can strike and damage another satellite.
sentences.zh: 例如，一种俄罗斯套娃式卫星，大卫星释放出一颗小卫星，小卫星释放出一种可以撞击并损坏另一颗卫星的装置。

sentences.en: There are machines with the ability to cast nets and extend grappling hooks, too.
sentences.zh: 还有能够投网和伸出抓钩的机器。

sentences.en: China, whose presence in space now far outpaces Russia's, is launching unmanned space planes into orbit, testing potentially unbreakable quantum communication links
sentences.zh: 中国在太空中的存在感现已远远超过俄罗斯，正在向轨道发射无人太空飞机，测试潜在的不可破解的量子通信链路，

sentences.en: and adding AI capabilities to satellites.
sentences.zh: 并为卫星增加人工智能能力。

sentences.en: An intelligence report, Lurch said, predicted the advent, within the next decade, of satellites with radio frequency jammers,
sentences.zh: 勒奇说，一份情报报告预测，在未来十年内，将出现带有射频干扰器、

sentences.en: chemical sprayers, and lasers that blind and disable the competition.
sentences.zh: 化学喷雾器和激光的卫星，用以致盲和瘫痪竞争对手。

sentences.en: All this would be in addition to the cyber warfare tools, electromagnetic instruments and ASAT anti-satellite missiles that already exist on the ground.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都将是地面上已有的网络战工具、电磁仪器和反卫星导弹之外的威胁。

sentences.en: In Lurch's assessment, space looked less like a grand new ocean for exploration, phrasing meant to induce wonder that is lingered from the Kennedy administration,
sentences.zh: 在勒奇的评估中，太空看起来不再像是一个宏大的探索新海洋——这个短语旨在激发人们自肯尼迪政府以来就留下的惊叹感——

sentences.en: and more like a robotic battlefield, where the conflicts raging on Earth would soon extend ever upward.
sentences.zh: 而更像是一个机器人战场，地球上肆虐的冲突很快就会延伸到上方。

sentences.en: The Space Force, the sixth and newest branch of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 太空军，美国第六个也是最新的军种，

sentences.en: military, was authorized by Congress and signed into law by President Donald Trump in December 2019.
sentences.zh: 由国会授权，并于2019年12月由唐纳德·特朗普总统签署成为法律。

sentences.en: Its creation was not a partisan endeavor, though Trump has boasted that the idea for the organization was his alone.
sentences.zh: 它的创建并非党派之争，尽管特朗普曾吹嘘该组织的构想完全出自他一人。

sentences.en: The initiative had, in fact, been shaped within the armed forces and Congress over the previous 25 years, based on the premise that, as satellite and space technologies evolved,
sentences.zh: 事实上，这一倡议在过去25年里一直在武装部队和国会内部酝酿，基于这样一个前提：随着卫星和太空技术的发展，

sentences.en: America's military organizations had to change as well.
sentences.zh: 美国的军事组织也必须随之改变。

sentences.en: At its incarnation, the Space Force was an assemblage of programs and teams that already existed, mainly as entities within the Air Force.
sentences.zh: 在成立之初，太空军是现有项目和团队的集合体，主要作为空军内部的实体存在。

sentences.en: It's one of the common misperceptions that it cost money to create the Space Force, and it really didn't, because we already had space forces,
sentences.zh: “一个常见的误解是创建太空军需要花钱，其实并没有，因为我们已经有了太空部队，”

sentences.en: Todd Harrison, of the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told me.
sentences.zh: 战略与国际研究中心的托德·哈里森告诉我。

sentences.en: These were just spread throughout the military, the people, the bases, the platforms, the satellites, the ground stations.
sentences.zh: 这些只是分散在军队各处，包括人员、基地、平台、卫星和地面站。

sentences.en: What the new directive did accomplish, however, was to group space endeavors under a central chain of command and authorize its leaders to chart a unified future.
sentences.zh: 然而，新指令确实实现了一点，即将太空事业归入一个中央指挥链，并授权其领导人规划一个统一的未来。

sentences.en: One of the things that we were lacking without a Space Force was an organization that would argue for its own destiny,
sentences.zh: “没有太空军时，我们缺少的一件事是一个会为自己的命运据理力争的组织，”

sentences.en: Douglas Levero, a former Pentagon official involved in helping start the branch, told me.
sentences.zh: 参与帮助启动该军种的前五角大楼官员道格拉斯·莱维罗告诉我。

sentences.en: The concern was that without a dedicated team within the military's bureaucracy that could push for the specific tools they needed, the United States would be at a disadvantage.
sentences.zh: 人们担心，如果军队官僚机构内部没有一个专门的团队来推动他们所需的特定工具，美国将处于不利地位。

sentences.en: Some strategists worried that the nation already was.
sentences.zh: 一些战略家担心国家已经处于这种境地。

sentences.en: Levero pointed out that two decades ago, a Chinese military analyst named Wang Hucheng wrote a paper that presaged an aspect of China's aerospace strategy.
sentences.zh: 莱维罗指出，二十年前，一位名叫王沪成的中国军事分析家写了一篇论文，预示了中国航空航天战略的一个方面。

sentences.en: For countries that can never win a war with the United States by using the method of tanks and planes, attacking the U.S.
sentences.zh: “对于那些永远无法通过坦克和飞机的方法赢得与美国战争的国家来说，攻击美国

sentences.en: space system may be an irresistible and most tempting choice.
sentences.zh: 太空系统可能是一个不可抗拒且最诱人的选择。”

sentences.en: The argument identified space as the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这一论点将太空确定为美国

sentences.en: military's soft ribs and strategic weakness.
sentences.zh: 军队的软肋和战略弱点。

sentences.en: From the start, the Space Force had detractors.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，太空军就有批评者。

sentences.en: Air Force officials wondered if it was necessary, while some political observers believed that it signified the start of a dangerous and expensive militarization of another realm.
sentences.zh: 空军官员怀疑它是否有必要，而一些政治观察家则认为，这标志着另一个领域危险且昂贵的军事化开始。

sentences.en: What seemed harder to argue against was how nearly every aspect of modern warfare and defense, intelligence, surveillance, communications, operations, missile detection,
sentences.zh: 似乎更难反驳的是，现代战争和防御的几乎每一个方面——情报、监视、通信、作战、导弹探测——

sentences.en: has come to rely on links to orbiting satellites.
sentences.zh: 都已经开始依赖与轨道卫星的连接。

sentences.en: The recent battles in Eastern Europe, in which Russia has tried to disrupt
sentences.zh: 最近在东欧发生的战斗，俄罗斯试图干扰

sentences.en: Ukraine's space-borne communication systems, are a case in point.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰的星载通信系统，就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: And yet, the strategic exploitation of space now extends well beyond military concerns.
sentences.zh: 然而，对太空的战略开发现在已经远远超出了军事范畴。

sentences.en: Satellite phone systems have become widespread.
sentences.zh: 卫星电话系统已经普及。

sentences.en: Positioning and timing satellites, such as GPS, now overseen by the Space Force, allow for digital mapping, navigation, banking, and agricultural management.
sentences.zh: 现在由太空军监管的定位和授时卫星（如GPS），实现了数字地图、导航、银行和农业管理。

sentences.en: A world without orbital weather surveys seems unthinkable.
sentences.zh: 一个没有轨道天气监测的世界似乎是不可想象的。

sentences.en: Modern life is reliant on space technologies to an extent that an interruption would create profound economic and social distress.
sentences.zh: 现代生活在很大程度上依赖于太空技术，以至于任何中断都会造成深远的经济和社会困扰。

sentences.en: The work of the Space Force is, by its nature, highly sensitive, often classified, and mostly out of sight.
sentences.zh: 太空军的工作本质上高度敏感，通常是机密的，而且大多处于视线之外。

sentences.en: This leaves the organization in a battle for visibility and, at times, viability.
sentences.zh: 这使得该组织在争取知名度，有时甚至是生存能力方面陷入了困境。

sentences.en: Some members of the Force, guardians, as they're called, told me that even now they find themselves bumping into members of other branches of the military who see their arm patches
sentences.zh: 一些太空军成员——也就是所谓的“守护者”——告诉我，即使是现在，他们也会遇到其他军种的成员，这些人看到他们的臂章，

sentences.en: and ask, in earnest,
sentences.zh: 并认真地问：

sentences.en: Space Force, is that a real thing?
sentences.zh: “太空军，那是真实存在的吗？”

sentences.en: The Steve Carell
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·卡瑞尔的

sentences.en: Netflix comedy series, which members of the actual Space Force sometimes argue is neither good nor funny, doesn't help their cause.
sentences.zh: Netflix喜剧系列剧——真正的太空军成员有时认为它既不好看也不好笑——对他们的事业毫无帮助。

sentences.en: It, likewise, doesn't capture their seriousness of purpose.
sentences.zh: 同样，它也没有捕捉到他们目标的严肃性。

sentences.en: For the moment, the Force has taken up a problem not often contemplated outside science fiction.
sentences.zh: 目前，太空军已经承担了一个在科幻小说之外不常被考虑的问题。

sentences.en: How do you fight a war in space or a war on Earth that expands into space?
sentences.zh: 你如何打一场太空战争，或者一场延伸到太空的地球战争？

sentences.en: And even if you're ready to fight, how do you make sure you don't have a space war in the first place?
sentences.zh: 即使你准备好战斗，你如何确保首先就不会发生太空战争？

sentences.en: The Space Force's
sentences.zh: 太空军的

sentences.zh: 作战部门总部位于科罗拉多斯普林斯东南部，在一栋巨大的三层建筑内，位于彼得森

sentences.en: Space Force Base.
sentences.zh: 太空军基地的警戒范围内。

sentences.en: Until recently, it was
sentences.zh: 直到最近，它还是

sentences.en: Peterson Air Force Base.
sentences.zh: 彼得森空军基地。

sentences.en: The office's inner workings are highly secure and secretive.
sentences.zh: 该办公室的内部运作高度安全且保密。

sentences.en: The Force, as one security analyst told me, has a larger proportion of its budget, around $26 billion this year, dedicated to classified spending than any other
sentences.zh: 正如一位安全分析师告诉我的，太空军预算中用于机密支出的比例——今年约为260亿美元——比其他任何

sentences.en: branch of the military.
sentences.zh: 军种都要高。

sentences.en: Visitors to headquarters are not allowed to bring electronic devices or walk unescorted inside.
sentences.zh: 总部访客不允许携带电子设备或在无人陪同的情况下在内部走动。

sentences.en: The building, nevertheless, hums with activity, with personnel hustling about under a canopy of scale-model satellites, large replicas of machines that now orbit Earth,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，大楼里依然忙碌，人员在明亮通风的中庭里穿梭，中庭悬挂着比例模型卫星，这些都是现在环绕地球运行的机器的大型复制品。

sentences.en: hanging in a bright, airy atrium.
sentences.zh: 悬挂在明亮、通风的中庭。

sentences.en: When I visited in late September, several military and civilian personnel took me through their day-to-day work.
sentences.zh: 当我在9月下旬访问时，几名军事和文职人员带我了解了他们的日常工作。

sentences.en: Right away, they noted that the Space Force is often mistaken for United States
sentences.zh: 他们立刻指出，太空军经常被误认为是美国

sentences.en: Space Command, also headquartered in Colorado, that reports to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 太空司令部，该司令部也设在科罗拉多州，直接向美国

sentences.en: Secretary of Defense.
sentences.zh: 国防部长汇报。
